sample_posts.text:
RWA capital is institutional even when buyer count looks retail
Arrakis' buyer classification makes the split hard to ignore: retail wallets are most of the buyers, but capital sits with a tiny institutional cohort. Wallets with ≥$1M make up just 4.2% of buyers, yet control 93% of the dollars — $38.8B. The identifiable $12.4B slice tells its own story: 66% from DAO/protocol treasuries, 15% individuals, 9% CEX custody, 6% market makers, 4% crypto funds.
So the marketing job is helping a small set of crypto-native allocators discover the product, evaluate the structure, and defend the allocation

> BTC rose 43% in Q3, but rising prices didn't bring more investment into crypto companies.
> Big lead VCs pulled back, while exchange-backed funds stepped up.
> Seed deals hit a two-year low as capital moved to Series A–C companies with proven revenue.
> M&A shifted to smaller deals that buy specific capabilities like licenses and payments, with deal value down 83%.
